content: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death globally, claiming more lives each year than any other condition. In 2019, out of 56 million deaths worldwide, 18 million were attributed to CVD. Hypertension (HTN) significantly increases the risk of diseases affecting the heart, brain, kidneys, and other organs. Approximately 1.28 billion people worldwide are affected by hypertension, yet only 23% of women and 18% of men have their condition under control. The guidelines for managing hypertension include the following recommendations: 1. Blood Pressure (BP) Threshold for Initiating Drug Treatment: For individuals diagnosed with hypertension and a BP of ≥140/≥90 mmHg, treatment is strongly recommended based on moderate to high-certainty evidence. For individuals with CVD and a systolic blood pressure (SBP) of 130–139 mmHg, treatment is also strongly recommended with moderate to high-certainty evidence. For individuals without CVD but with high CVD risk, diabetes, or chronic kidney disease (CKD) and an SBP of 130–139 mmHg, treatment is conditionally recommended based on moderate to high-certainty evidence. 2. Screening and Assessment Before Treatment: Screening for comorbidities and conducting a cardiovascular risk assessment is recommended, provided it does not delay the initiation of treatment. This recommendation is conditional and based on low-certainty evidence. 3. Choice of Antihypertensive Drugs: The use of any of the following drug classes is strongly recommended: diuretics, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEi), angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs), or calcium channel blockers (CCBs). This recommendation is supported by high-certainty evidence. 4. Combination Therapy: To improve adherence and persistence, combination therapy is recommended, preferably in a single-pill formulation. This is a conditional recommendation based on moderate-certainty evidence. 5. Target BP for Hypertension Control: For individuals without comorbidities, the target BP is <140/90 mmHg. For individuals with CVD, the target SBP is <130 mmHg. For individuals with high CVD risk, diabetes, or CKD, the target SBP is <130 mmHg. These recommendations are strong and supported by moderate-certainty evidence. 6. Follow-Up Intervals: Monthly follow-ups are recommended until the target BP is achieved. Once the target BP is reached, follow-ups every 3–6 months are recommended. These are conditional recommendations based on low-certainty evidence. 7. Involvement of Non-Physician Healthcare Workers: Hypertension management can be provided by trained non-physician healthcare workers who are authorized to prescribe medications and follow management protocols under physician oversight. This is a conditional recommendation based on low-certainty evidence. These guidelines are published by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2022, with electronic and print versions available under ISBN 978-92-4-005096-9 and ISBN 978-92-4-005097-6, respectively.
